ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The diagram shows an urban rainwater utilization system. On the left there are a road, a stormwater inlet, and pipes. After rainwater enters the pipes from the road stormwater inlet, it flows in sequence through treatment facilities such as an initial runoff pond, a sedimentation chamber, and a filtration chamber. On the right side of the diagram there is a deep well labeled "well". The water flow after the filtration chamber leads to this well. Arrows are drawn in the lower part of the well pointing toward the underground direction, indicating that the water infiltrates underground. Then reason: What the deep well on the right receives is rainwater that has undergone treatment such as sedimentation and filtration, and the arrows in the diagram show that the water enters underground from the well, rather than being discharged into a river or directly supplied for use on the ground. Therefore, the function of this deep well is to recharge the treated rainwater into the underground aquifer, that is, to recharge groundwater.
